# 1 Maccabees Chapter 14 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)

**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Codex Sinaiticus, 1 Maccabees 14 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-DC/1MA_014_page_001.jpg

---

**1** In 140 BCE, Demetrius II mustered his army and marched into Media looking for reinforcements to use against Trypho.

**2** But Arsaces, king of Persia and Media, heard that Demetrius had crossed into his territory and sent one of his generals to bring him in alive.

**3** The general engaged Demetrius's forces, broke them, captured Demetrius, and handed him to Arsaces, who put him in custody.

**4** Judea knew peace throughout Simon's reign. He worked for his people's good, and they delighted in his leadership and in his glory all his days.

---

*[Verses 5–15: An encomium — a formal poem of praise — embedded in the narrative.]*

**5** Among all his glorious deeds:
    he seized Joppa as a harbor
    and opened the gate to the islands of the sea.

**6** He pushed the nation's borders outward
    and made himself master of the land.

**7** He brought home many captives
    and took control of Gazara, Beth-zur, and the citadel —
    purging each of its defilements.
    No one stood against him.

**8** The people farmed their land in peace,
    and the earth gave back its harvest,
    the trees of the plain their fruit.

**9** The old men gathered in the squares
    and spoke together of the good times,
    while the young men dressed in military glory.

**10** He kept the cities supplied
    and made them strong —
    until his name rang out to the ends of the earth.

**11** He made peace in the land.
    Israel's joy was unbounded.

**12** Every man sat safe
    beneath his own vine,
    beneath his own fig tree,
    with no one to frighten him.

**13** No enemy remained in the land to attack them.
    The kings were crushed in those days.

**14** He stood up for the poor of his people.
    He enforced the law.
    He hunted down every lawbreaker and scoundrel.

**15** He adorned the sanctuary
    and filled it with sacred vessels.

---

**16** Word reached Rome and Sparta that Jonathan had died, and they grieved.

**17** Then they heard that his brother Simon had taken his place as high priest and was governing the country and its cities.

**18** They wrote to him on bronze tablets — renewing the friendship and alliance they had made with his brothers Judas and Jonathan.

**19** The letters were read aloud before the assembly in Jerusalem.

**20** The Spartan letter read: "The rulers and the city of Sparta — to Simon the great priest, the elders, the priests, and the rest of the Jewish people, our brothers, greetings.

**21** The envoys you sent to us reported your glory and honor, and we were glad when they arrived.

**22** Their message has been officially recorded in our public decrees: Numenius son of Antiochus and Antipater son of Jason, Jewish envoys, came to us to renew friendship with us.

**23** We voted to receive them with honor and to archive their words, so that the Spartan people would have a permanent record of it. And a copy of this has been sent to you, Simon."

**24** After this, Simon sent Numenius to Rome carrying a massive golden shield — a thousand minas in weight — to seal the alliance with the Romans.

**25** When all this became known, the people asked: "How do we ever repay Simon and his sons?

**26** He and his brothers and his father's house have kept Israel standing against her enemies and won her freedom." They had it inscribed on bronze tablets and mounted on pillars on Mount Zion.

**27** The inscription reads: "On the eighteenth of Elul, 140 BCE — the third year of Simon the great high priest —

**28** in Asaramel, in a great assembly of priests, people, national leaders, and elders, the following was publicly proclaimed:

**29** Many wars have troubled our land. Simon son of Mattathias, of the priestly house of Joarib, and his brothers put themselves in harm's way and stood up to our nation's enemies, in order to protect the sanctuary and uphold the law. They have brought great glory to their nation.

**30** Jonathan reorganized the nation and served as its high priest, and was then gathered to his people.

**31** When their enemies attempted to invade and desecrate the sanctuary,

**32** Simon stepped forward. He financed the fight himself, armed the nation's warriors, and paid their wages.

**33** He built up Judea's cities and fortified Beth-zur on the southern border — previously an enemy weapons cache — and stationed Jewish soldiers there.

**34** He fortified Joppa on the coast and Gazara near the border of Azotus — both formerly enemy strongholds — settled Jews in them, and provided everything needed to rebuild them.

**35** The people saw Simon's faithfulness and recognized the glory he was bringing to the nation. They made him their leader and high priest — for his righteousness, his loyalty, and his constant striving to lift his people higher.

**36** Under his leadership, the country prospered. The Gentiles were cleared from the land. The men in the Davidic citadel — who had been a constant source of pollution and harassment to the sanctuary — were cleared out too.

**37** He settled Jews there, fortified it for the defense of the land and the city, and heightened the walls of Jerusalem.

**38** For all this, King Demetrius confirmed him as high priest

**39** and enrolled him as a royal friend, honoring him greatly.

**40** Demetrius had heard that the Romans had formally declared the Jews to be friends, allies, and brothers, and had received Simon's envoys with honor.

**41** It was then formally decreed that Simon should be high priest and leader of the Jews permanently — until a trustworthy prophet should come —

**42** and that he would hold full military command, with authority over the sanctuary, over public appointments, over the land, arms, and fortresses;

**43** that all public documents in the country should be dated by his name; that he should wear purple and the gold ornament;

**44** and that no one — priest or layman — could override his decrees, call any assembly without his consent, or wear purple or the gold clasp.

**45** Anyone who violated any of these provisions would be liable to punishment.

**46** The whole people approved these arrangements. Simon accepted them gladly, agreeing to serve as high priest, commander, and ethnarch of the Jews and priests — their protector in all things.

**47** Orders were given to engrave all this on bronze tablets and mount them in a prominent place in the sanctuary precinct,

**48** and to place copies in the treasury, so that Simon and his sons would have them on record.
